key_insight: The paper shows that backward mapping from desired device targets to chemically interpretable descriptors can identify phase-stable, lead-free double perovskites with DFT-validated properties.
engineering_relevance: This provides an interpretable inverse-design workflow for screening large halide perovskite spaces and accelerating selection of safer, stable materials for optoelectronic devices.
method: Filter 13,088 charge-balanced A2BB'X6 compositions with halide-aware geometric formability rules.
Encode compounds with six chemical-genome descriptor families and train evolutionary-optimized ML surrogates for stability and band gap.
Use SHAP interpretation plus DFT phenotype closure to validate top candidates and extract design rules.
evidence_signal: The workflow narrows the search to seven DFT-validated candidates and evaluates them for stability, band structure, effective mass, dielectric response, optical absorption, conductivity, reflectivity, energy loss, and XRD fingerprints.
watch_item: Because the band-gap surrogate is trained on scalar-relativistic PBE labels, practical deployment may need higher-level corrections and experimental validation of synthesized phases.
paper_title: Backward Mapping from Device Targets to Chemical Genomes for Interpretable Discovery of Phase-Stable Lead-Free Double Perovskites with DFT-Validated Design Rules
